long_biography.plain_text:
David Dein moved from food importing and sugar trading into football when he acquired a substantial Arsenal shareholding in 1983. As vice-chairman, he combined ownership with hands-on club administration, helped drive the formation of the Premier League and recruited Arsène Wenger. He also held senior roles with the Football Association, UEFA and the G-14 group of European clubs.

After leaving Arsenal and selling his remaining stake, Dein continued as a football ambassador, adviser, author and speaker. He founded the Twinning Project to connect professional clubs with prisons, using coaching, qualifications and mentoring to improve employment prospects for people approaching release. That work extends a career built on promoting football as both a commercial institution and a source of social opportunity.
